classification.difficultyReason: Apply the tangent–secant product rule, express the whole secant using its two segments, and reject a negative length when solving the quadratic in part c.

content.prompt: $PT$ is a tangent to a circle where $T$ is the point of tangency, and $PXY$ is a secant.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If $PT=6\text{ cm}$ and $PX=4\text{ cm}$, find $XY$ and $PY$.

answer.worked:
Using the tangent–secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}PX\times PY&=PT^2\\4\times PY&=6^2\\PY&=9\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Since $X$ lies between $P$ and $Y$,
$$\begin{align*}XY&=PY-PX\\XY&=9-4\\XY&=5\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}PY&=PX+XY\\PY&=3+24\\PY&=27\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
Using the tangent–secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}PT^2&=PX\times PY\\PT^2&=3\times27\\PT^2&=81\\PT&=9\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$PX=4\text{ cm}$.

Use $PY=PX+21$ in the tangent–secant product rule and take the positive solution.
answer.worked:
Let $PX=x\text{ cm}$, so $PY=(x+21)\text{ cm}$. Using the tangent–secant product rule,
$$\begin{align*}PX\times PY&=PT^2\\x(x+21)&=10^2\\x^2+21x&=100\\x^2+21x-100&=0\\(x+25)(x-4)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Thus $x=-25$ or $x=4$. A length is positive, so $PX=4\text{ cm}$.
